target.title: End-to-End Audio-Visual Speech Recognition with Conformers
target.venue: Not stated on the paper's first page

read.pdf: All 5 pages inspected, including Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Tables 1-4, and the complete reference list

entries.text: The proposed AVSR model is trained end-to-end from raw visual pixels and audio waveforms using ResNet-18, Conformer encoders, MLP fusion, and hybrid CTC/attention.
entries.condition: Audio-only, visual-only, and audio-visual model variants; sentence transcription
entries.quote: In this work, we present a hybrid CTC/Attention model based on a ResNet-18 and Convolution-augmented transformer (Conformer), that can be trained in an end-to-end manner.

entries.text: Novelty claim: jointly integrating feature extraction with the CTC/attention back-end improves on the authors' earlier two-stage model.
entries.condition: Compared with the previous audio-visual model [25] using pre-computed visual features

entries.text: The authors claim replacing recurrent networks with Conformers further advances state-of-the-art performance.
entries.condition: Architectural substitution in the proposed recognition system

entries.text: The authors claim a transformer language model improves performance over an RNN language model.
entries.condition: Language-model replacement; later decoding uses shallow fusion
entries.quote: Finally, we replace the RNN-based Language Model (RNN-LM) with a transformer-based LM which enhances the performance even more.

entries.text: The abstract claims large state-of-the-art gains in audio-only, visual-only, and audio-visual recognition.
entries.condition: LRS2 and LRS3; all three modalities

entries.text: The introduction claims state-of-the-art gains on both datasets, including over methods trained on much larger external datasets.
entries.condition: LRS2 and LRS3; datasets and comparison methods differ across table rows

entries.text: The authors claim AVSR gains over audio-only recognition increase under heavy background noise.
entries.condition: Babble-noise SNR sweep; both audio-only and audio-visual models are described as noise-augmented

entries.text: The encoders learn features directly from unprocessed input pixels and waveforms.
entries.condition: Visual and acoustic input streams

entries.text: Visual front-end: modified ResNet-18 with a 3D first convolution, global-average spatial pooling, and a 5×7×7 kernel.
entries.condition: Raw video mouth-region frames

entries.text: Audio front-end: 1D ResNet-18; first filter size is 80 samples (5 ms), first-block stride 4, later block stride 2, output 25 frames/s.
entries.condition: Raw waveform; downsampled to match the visual frame rate

entries.text: The visual front-end uses 68 tracked facial landmarks and a 96×96 mouth ROI, then training-time random crops of 88×88.
entries.condition: Landmarks detected/tracked per video; random crop used for each training image sequence

entries.text: Video patches are grayscale and normalized using the training-set overall mean and variance; each raw waveform is mean-centered and divided by its standard deviation.
entries.condition: Exact statistics, scope of training set, and test-time application are not specified

entries.text: Training video augmentation uses random 88×88 crops and horizontal flips with probability 0.5.
entries.condition: Each image sequence during training

entries.text: Training audio augmentation includes NOISEX babble at −5, 0, 5, 10, 15, or 20 dB SNR; a noise level or clean audio is selected uniformly.
entries.condition: Babble noise from NOISEX; selection among listed SNRs or clean audio is uniform
entries.quote: The selection of one of the noise levels or the use of a clean waveform is done using a uniform distribution.

entries.text: Audio augmentation zeros two consecutive-sample segments up to 0.4 s and rejects two consecutive frequency bands up to 150 Hz wide.
entries.condition: Time-domain audio augmentation; details of segment sampling are not provided

entries.text: Audio-only experiments additionally use speed perturbation from 0.9× to 1.1× speed.
entries.condition: Audio-only training experiments

entries.text: The back-end has 12 Conformer blocks, d_ff=2048, d_k=d_v=256, 4 heads for visual-only and 8 for audio-only/AV; depthwise kernel size 31; decoder has 6 attention blocks.
entries.condition: Modality-specific head count as stated; decoder feed-forward and attention dimensions match encoder

entries.text: End-to-end training uses Adam (β1=.9, β2=.98, ε=10−9), batch size 8, 25,000-step linear warm-up to 0.0004, inverse-square-root decay, and 50 epochs.
entries.unit: batch examples; steps; peak learning rate; epochs
entries.condition: Whole network; utterances over 600 frames in pre-training set excluded

entries.text: The network is randomly initialized except for some experiments using LRW-pretrained encoder front-ends; pre-training utterances longer than 600 frames are excluded.
entries.condition: LRW initialization applies only in some experiments; exact initialization variants are tabulated

entries.text: The model predicts character sequences with a hybrid CTC/attention objective that trades off the two log-likelihoods using α.
entries.condition: The paper defines α but does not give its selected value

entries.text: Recognition output is characters, trained with the combined CTC and attention mechanisms.
entries.condition: Specific character inventory and tokenization are not supplied

entries.text: A transformer LM is trained for 10 epochs on LibriSpeech and LRS2/LRS3 pre-training and training transcripts, totaling 16.2 million words; shallow-fusion weights are λ=0.1 and β=0.6.
entries.unit: epochs; words; CTC weight; LM weight
entries.condition: LibriSpeech transcripts (960 h) plus LRS2/LRS3 pre-training and training transcripts
entries.quote: In our work, we set λ to 0.1 and β to 0.6, respectively.

entries.text: LRS2 has 224.1 h and 144,482 BBC clips; its listed partitions are 195 h pre-training, 28 h train, 0.6 h validation, and 0.5 h test.
entries.condition: LRS2; split utterance counts are detailed in t24

entries.text: LRS2 partitions contain 96,318 pre-training, 45,839 training, 1,082 validation, and 1,243 test utterances.
entries.condition: LRS2; corresponding durations are recorded in t23

entries.text: LRS3 contains 151,819 TED/TEDx utterances totaling 438.9 h; 408 h pre-training, 30 h training-validation, and 0.9 h test.
entries.condition: LRS3 dataset partitions as described by paper

entries.text: LRS3 partitions contain 118,516 pre-training, 31,982 training-validation, and 1,321 test utterances.
entries.condition: LRS3; the paper does not state a separate validation split within training-validation

entries.text: Some target experiments initialize front-end modules using publicly available LRW-pretrained models; the paper's footnote links model weights, not a code repository.
entries.unit: hours of LRW in comparison tables
entries.condition: Only some experiments use LRW initialization; public link is https://sites.google.com/view/audiovisual-speech-recognition

entries.text: Primary reported metric is WER on LRS2/LRS3; tables do not specify whether the headline results are clean-test or noise-corrupted-test scores.
entries.condition: Tables 3 and 4; clean/noisy evaluation protocol not explicitly stated for each reported result
entries.quote: Table 3. Word Error Rate (WER) of the audio-only, visual-only and audio-visual models on LRS2.

entries.text: No random seeds, number of independent runs, or run-to-run variability are reported.
entries.condition: Applies to training and all reported WER results
entries.quote: The whole network is trained for 50 epochs.

entries.text: The paper names the LRS2 test split but does not report speaker counts, identities, or whether LRS2 training/pre-training speakers overlap its test speakers.
entries.condition: LRS2 evaluation

entries.text: Although LRS3v0.4 is described as speaker-independent, counts/identities of speakers and split-level overlap verification are not reported.
entries.condition: LRS3v0.4 evaluation

entries.text: The paper reports a LRS2 validation partition and LRS3 training-validation partition but does not say how they are used for checkpoint selection, hyperparameter tuning, or early stopping.
entries.condition: Model selection and evaluation protocol

entries.text: Normalization is mentioned, but exact visual mean/variance values, the scope of statistics, and test-time application are unspecified; log-Mel normalization details are also absent.
entries.condition: Visual training-set mean/variance and per-waveform mean/std are described generally

entries.text: No chance-level or random-transcription baseline is reported for the WER task.
entries.condition: LRS2/LRS3 benchmark results

entries.text: The target is described as characters, but the character set, word/token segmentation, text normalization, and WER scoring conventions (case, punctuation, and number handling) are not specified.
entries.condition: All reported WER scores

entries.text: Beam/search strategy, beam width, length penalties, and other decoding settings are not reported; λ and β are reported separately in t22.
entries.condition: Hybrid CTC/attention decoding and shallow-fusion language model
entries.quote: The weighted prior score from the language model is incorporated through a shallow fusion, which is described in Eq. 2.

entries.text: Per-row use of the transformer LM is not identified for all results tables, and no decoding-time LM/data-matching details are provided beyond the general shallow-fusion description.
entries.condition: Tables 2-4; LM corpus and global fusion weights are given in t22
entries.quote: The weighted prior score from the language model is incorporated through a shallow fusion, which is described in Eq. 2.

entries.text: For Fig. 2, exact per-SNR WER values, test-noise sampling, noise recording identity, and whether test noise is independent of training augmentation are not reported.
entries.condition: Babble noise sweep at stated SNR values; only the maximum raw-vs-log-Mel margin is numerically specified

entries.text: The CTC/attention training loss coefficient α is defined but its chosen value is not reported.
entries.condition: Training objective in Eq. 1
entries.quote: L =αlogpCTC(y|x)+(1−α)logpCE(y|x) (1)

entries.text: No inference latency, throughput, hardware, memory, or online/deployment evaluation is reported.
entries.condition: Paper reports benchmark recognition results rather than deployed-system measurements

questions.q: Does the paper's claim that its visual-only LRS3 model outperforms other methods hold for the tabulated results?
questions.answer: Not for the displayed WER comparison: the target's best speaker-independent LRS3v0.4 visual-only score is 43.3%, whereas Table 4 lists RNN-T at 33.6% WER. The target uses much less listed training data, but lower WER is better; the paper's broad superiority wording is therefore not supported by that row.

questions.q: Which LRS3 results are affected by known speaker overlap?
questions.answer: The LRS3v0.0 numbers (30.4% visual-only, 1.3% audio-only, and 1.2% audio-visual) use a version where speakers overlap between pre-training and test; the authors explicitly attribute the improved scores partly to that overlap. The v0.4 rows are described as speaker-independent.

questions.q: Can the LRS2/LRS3 headline WER values be unambiguously interpreted as clean-test performance, and are repeatability details available?
questions.answer: The tables identify the benchmarks and modalities but do not explicitly state the clean/noisy status for each headline row. No seeds, repeated runs, or variability estimates are reported. The paper separately describes a babble-noise SNR plot, without tabulating its exact per-SNR values or test-noise sampling details.

questions.q: What evaluation and decoding details remain unspecified despite the reported scores?
questions.answer: The paper omits split-level speaker counts/overlap verification for LRS2, checkpoint/validation selection procedures, exact normalization statistics and test-time use, chance baseline, character inventory and WER normalization, and beam/search settings. It defines the training loss coefficient α but gives no value; it gives general shallow-fusion weights but does not map LM use to every table row.

questions.q: What does the authors' stated caveat imply about the fusion mechanism?
questions.answer: Their conclusion proposes adaptive modality weighting as future work; the evaluated MLP fusion therefore does not learn a noise-conditioned modality weight in the reported system.
